work_order.approach: Fix the two QA-proven root causes with different approaches from attempt 1, and carry forward that attempt's two passing fixes unchanged. BUG-1: Field generates its input id from the field name alone (field-${name}), so the members page renders two inputs with id field-name and fills/submits hit the wrong one. Field now derives a unique id per instance with React useId so each label targets exactly its own input; RenameGroupForm keeps its state.ok refresh effect, which becomes observable once the submit is fixed. BUG-2: RemoveButton called router.refresh() in the awaited continuation of the wrapped Server Action, before useActionState commits the ok state that renders the status. RemoveButton now follows the ArchiveButton precedent exactly: the wrapped action only returns the result, and a useEffect on state.ok commits the 'Removed <name>.' status render first and then calls router.refresh() once (announced-ref guarded). The money sign-carry and readMembers EXISTS-predicate fixes from attempt 1 passed QA (T-1, T-2) and are carried forward unchanged.

work_order.root_cause: Two wrong diagnoses in attempt 1, both proven by QA evidence. (1) Rename: the plan blamed a missing router.refresh, but QA captured the Server Action request carrying the field's INITIAL value on the base commit — refresh can never fix a submit that sends the wrong value. The true cause is a duplicate DOM id: Field builds id as field-${name}, and the members page renders two Field name='name' inputs, so fills land in the placeholder field and Save submits the rename form's untouched value with a false 'Saved.'. (2) Removal: the plan assumed the status insertion commits before the async refresh lands, but the PR calls router.refresh() in the action's awaited continuation BEFORE useActionState commits the ok state — on a fast connection the refresh wins and the row unmounts with zero insertions, exactly QA's intermittent signature.

work_order.understanding: Attempt 1 (previous-work-order.json v1, PR #21) was wrong on both browser defects, and QA's evidence proves it. First, the plan diagnosed rename staleness as a missing router.refresh(); but QA captured the Server Action body carrying the INITIAL name on base commit 7390e3e, and the T-7/T-4 trees show the typed value in the placeholder 'Name' input while the rename input kept the old value with a false 'Saved.'. The true cause is Field's id = field-${name} colliding across the two same-named fields on the members page. Second, the plan assumed the 'Removed' insertion commits before the refresh; but the PR dispatches router.refresh() in the wrapped action's continuation before useActionState commits ok state, so the refresh intermittently wins (T-9/T-10/T-11). The money and readMembers fixes passed QA and are carried forward; only the Field-id and removal-ordering approaches change.

validated_work_order.approach: Fix all five review findings per the binding route decision (implementer variant B for the remove ordering bug): carry the sign outside the whole part in formatMinor; express the member-list read as a membership join inside the fetching query; give Field per-instance unique ids via useId; convert RemoveButton to an effect on the committed ok state that renders the confirmation and calls router.refresh(), and remove revalidatePath('/', 'layout') from removeMember only (documented as the deliberate exception since every route is dynamic); add router.refresh() on rename success; audit every other control that unmounts on success for the same ordering bug.
assumptions: Every route that renders group data is dynamic (verified: no generateStaticParams, force-static, or cached fetches under src/app; every page reads the session), so dropping the server revalidate in removeMember does not leave a statically cached page stale; AC-4 guards this behaviorally.
The duplicate-id collision is the members screen's two Field name="name" instances (AddPlaceholderForm label Name + RenameGroupForm label Group name) sharing id field-name.
readMembers can reuse the existing memberOfGroup EXISTS predicate in the fetch WHERE clause without changing its null-for-non-member contract.

validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: All five root causes were re-verified at their exact lines on main, the binding decision settles the one contested mechanism (variant B, proven by the implementer's 3x browser runs plus the decisive no-refresh control run), and I independently confirmed the every-route-is-dynamic premise the revalidate removal rests on. residual_risks: RemoveButton confirmation is transient by design: the refreshed list unmounts the row, so a screen reader that has not yet announced the inserted status loses it; the row's disappearance is the durable signal.
Remove and rename refresh only the current tab; a stale row in another tab still submits and surfaces the action's formError.
If the post-remove client refresh itself fails, the 'Removed <name>.' status shows while the stale row remains with its button disabled and no retry; a manual reload recovers.
risks: Removing the removeMember revalidate relies on every route being dynamic; verified structurally (no static markers under src/app) with the home-freshness criterion (AC-4) as the behavioral guard.

The readMembers rewrite reuses the memberOfGroup SQL predicate in a SELECT where clause; if the Drizzle union Session type rejects it there, fall back to an aliased self-join and keep the single-round-trip property.

RenameGroupForm's refresh delivers a new initialName through the existing sync effect, which overwrites in-progress typing raced between submit and refresh landing; the success path (typed name equals new name) is unaffected.

validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #20 carries five unfixed review findings from PR #19 (for #4): (1) formatMinor drops '-' for sub-one-unit negatives, (2) readMembers authorises via a separate check-then-fetch instead of an in-query membership join, (3) RemoveButton shows nothing on success until reload, (4) rename shows Saved. while server-rendered names stay stale until reload, plus the duplicate-Field-id root cause behind the rename submit carrying the initial value and the remove ordering bug behind the missing confirmation. The binding route decision adopts variant B (drop revalidatePath from removeMember, refresh from the committed ok-state effect), keeps the unique-Field-ids and AC-1/AC-2 fixes, and requires a home-list-freshness criterion plus an audit of other unmounting controls.
unknowns: Whether any supported currency's en-US formatToParts places the minus other than as a simple prefix; mitigated by reading the minus part from the formatter rather than hardcoding position.
Whether the readMembers join rewrite affects member ordering or placeholder-name coalescing in any edge case current tests do not pin.
